summary: Backend regression testing for the admin-device-exemption fix. Created new pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_admin_device_exempt.py covering all 5 review scenarios. All 5 tests PASS. The fix in server.py (~line 518) correctly (a) allows admin role (MOFEED, admin, MOF) to log in from any device without persisting bound_device, (b) still device-binds non-admin users on first login and returns 403 on a mismatched second device, and (c) leaves the /api/users/{uid}/unbind-device endpoint returning ok:true.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3547 lines — should be split into modules (auth, users, sales, etc.) for maintainability.

Device-binding uses role check `role == 'admin'`. If future admin-equivalent roles are added (e.g., 'super_admin'), this branch must be updated. Consider a permission-based check or a helper is_privileged(user).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix verified end-to-end: admin role is exempt from device binding, normal users still bound. Unbind endpoint intact. Frontend PublicOrder header test was in the review list but marked as backend-only testing_type; frontend behaviour not re-verified this iteration (already covered in iteration 7-8).
rca of the issue: Prior behaviour bound the FIRST successful admin login to a device and returned 403 on a mismatched second device. Fix adds `is_admin = user.get('role') == 'admin'` and gates both the mismatch check and the bound_device write with `not is_admin`, so admins are never bound. Verified in /app/backend/server.py lines 515-529.
